at 2026-07-15T12:00:00Z

# Git keeps the selection in each worktree's private administrative directory.
mkdir repo
exec git -C repo init -b main
exec sh -c 'printf "initial\n" > repo/README.md'
exec card --store repo/.git/.cardamom init --prefix git- --board-name 'Default board'
exec sh -c 'printf "version: 1\nissue:\n  id:\n    prefix: git-\n    strategy: sequential\n" > repo/.git/.cardamom/config.yaml'
exec card --store repo/.git/.cardamom board create 'Second board'
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/second-board.txt
exec git -C repo add README.md
exec git -C repo commit -m initial

cd repo
exec card board use board_00000000000000000000
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/use-default.txt
exists .git/cardamom-board
exec git worktree add ../linked -b linked
cd ../linked
exec card board use board_11111111111111111111
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/use-second.txt
exists ../repo/.git/worktrees/linked/cardamom-board
exec card create 'Linked issue'
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/linked-issue.txt

cd ../repo
exec card create 'Primary issue'
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/primary-issue.txt

# Non-Git selection lives beside the discovered .cardamom entry, not in a child cwd.
cd ..
mkdir plain
exec card --store plain/.cardamom init --prefix plain- --board-name 'Default board'
exec sh -c 'printf "version: 1\nissue:\n  id:\n    prefix: plain-\n    strategy: sequential\n" > plain/.cardamom/config.yaml'
exec card --store plain/.cardamom board create 'Second board'
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/second-board.txt
mkdir plain/a
mkdir plain/a/b
cd plain/a/b
exec card board use board_11111111111111111111
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/use-second.txt
exists ../../.cardamom-board
! exists .cardamom-board
exec card create 'Nested issue'
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/nested-issue.txt

-- golden/second-board.txt --
board_11111111111111111111
-- golden/use-default.txt --
using board_00000000000000000000 (Default board)
-- golden/use-second.txt --
using board_11111111111111111111 (Second board)
-- golden/linked-issue.txt --
git-1
-- golden/primary-issue.txt --
git-2
-- golden/nested-issue.txt --
plain-1
